title: AI Literacy in K-12 and Higher Education in the Wake of Generative AI: An Integrative Review
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapidly expanding but still loosely defined area of AI literacy, especially in the period after generative AI became widely available. The authors argue that the field contains many different uses of the term “AI literacy,” ranging from technical machine-learning instruction to prompt engineering with ChatGPT to critical discussions of AI ethics and societal impact. Their main goal is not to evaluate a single intervention, but to synthesize and organize the conceptual diversity in the literature.

Using an integrative review method, the paper examines 124 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and July 2024 that focused on AI literacy in K-12 or undergraduate contexts. The authors code studies according to how they conceptualize AI (technical details, tools, sociocultural impact) and literacy (functional, critical, indirectly beneficial). They identify established pre-generative-AI patterns, such as K-12 machine-learning curricula and ethics-focused lessons, and emerging post-generative-AI patterns, especially the teaching of generative AI tool use and prompt engineering.

The review includes K-12 and higher education studies across multiple countries, but it is not a primary outcome study and does not test subgroup effects or literacy outcomes directly. Its main conclusion is that the field needs more precise terminology and that generative AI has shifted AI literacy toward more tool-oriented and functionally framed instruction, while critical and sociocultural work remains important but less common in some areas. The paper also notes several research gaps, including limited postsecondary research, relatively few critical uses of AI tools, and the need for clearer conceptual boundaries within AI literacy research.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic large language model / generative AI chatbot or tool used for interactive text generation, prompting, and AI literacy instruction; no single commercial product is the focus of the review.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is an integrative review of 124 AI literacy studies in K-12 and higher education published since 2020, synthesizing how studies conceptualize AI and literacy. It does not evaluate a single AI tool; rather, it discusses generative AI tools in general, including unnamed LLM-based tools and examples such as ChatGPT.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an integrative review and conceptual framework paper, not an empirical evaluation of an AI intervention. It does not report primary outcome data, subgroup analyses, or effect estimates for a specific tool.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper is influential for framing AI literacy research and identifying trends, but it does not present measurable student outcome effects. As a review, its impact is conceptual rather than intervention-based.
